newsitem.title: USA: Natgas futures remain range-bound in slow trade.
newsitem.headline: Natgas futures remain range-bound in slow trade.

text.p: NYMEX Henry Hub natgas futures remained stuck in a range in sluggish Thursday afternoon trade, supported by firm cash prices and October's ability to bounce off the lows earlier, industry sources said.

At 1433 EDT, October was up 2.9 cents at $1.835 per million British thermal units after hitting a high of $1.855 earlier. November remained one cent lower at $2.02. The Oct/Nov spread narrowed further to 18.5 cents.
"Cash was trading flat to just over the screen. This gave good support to the market. It (October) bounced off $1.795 and filled the gap to $1.85," said one trader.
Most traders speculated the market was waiting for more signals from cash when trading resumes Friday morning before moving in either direction.

Cash prices on the U.S. Gulf Coast pipes were talked in the low-to-mid $1.80s, while in the Midcontinent prices were also stable in the mid-$1.60s to about $1.70. At the New York city-gate, gas sold in the low-$2 area.
Traders pegged support in October in the high-$1.70s, then the $1.73-1.74 area. Further support was seen at $1.68. Resistance was seen at $1.913, Tuesday's high.
At 1400 EDT, NYMEX said 20,851 Henry Hub contracts traded.
NYMEX's October Permian contract climbed a half-cent to $1.535. A total of 20 contracts traded as of 1400 EDT.
Physical prices carried about a five-cent premium to October futures in the high-$1.50s to low-$1.60s.
On the KCBT, October extended its gains to $1.630, up 3.4 cents, despite the gradual softness in physicals. The East/West spread widened by a half-cent to 20.5 cents (NYMEX premium).
Cash prices at Waha eased by more than five cents to the high-$1.60s, traders said.
